name: Tirhanah
overview: Tirhanah is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) and Maacah. His identity is grounded in his lineage within the tribe of Judah, a significant tribe in the biblical narrative. No additional notes are provided about his life or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Tirhanah appears only once in Scripture without a given meaning or divine origin. It is a proper name recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:48, and no further significance is indicated.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Tirhanah as the son of Chelubai (Caleb) and Maacah, establishing his place within the Judahite genealogy. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Tirhanah's significance lies chiefly in his genealogical connection to Caleb, a prominent figure in the tribe of Judah. His mention in 1 Chronicles 2:48 serves to preserve the lineage and heritage important to the biblical record of God's chosen people. While not noted for individual deeds, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in sustaining the tribe of Judah through successive generations.
